text:
Zoe: hey all, first-day panic :sweat_smile: trying to land the onboarding PR but both Buildkite and GH Actions are failing. not sure who to ping for repo/app/runner perms.

Kobe: welcome Zoe! paste the errors, quick triage.

Zoe: Buildkite immediately errors with: 
```
install_buildkite_github_app: pipeline does not have access to repository (403)
fatal: could not fetch refs
```
and GH Actions shows: 
```
This workflow is not allowed to access secrets.
Secrets are not available to this workflow.
```

Nima: hmm two classic causes: 1) Buildkite GitHub App isn't installed or the repo wasn't added to the app. 2) GH Actions secrets blocked by env protection or org allowlist. Are you opening the PR from a fork?

Zoe: in-repo branch on github.com/redwood-inference/client-examples. Also my local build step tries to push a test image to GCR, so the CI does a docker push.

ci-bot: Note: Organization policy "Allow actions and reusable workflows from" is set to "Only selected repositories".

Kobe: ok. For Buildkite there are two ways: add the repo to the GitHub App install (preferred) or configure a deploy key on the repo and add that to the pipeline. For GH Actions, check repo -> Settings -> Actions and Environments. If the secret is scoped to an environment that requires approvals, the workflow won't get it.

Zoe: checked Environments -> staging: it requires reviewers. I can't approve since I'm new. Also noticed the workflow uses: runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, gpu] but our self-hosted pool only has 'gpu-run' label. so runner label mismatch might cause the GH job to be queued forever earlier.

Nima: good catch on runner labels. For onboarding we usually change runs-on to ubuntu-latest to avoid label mismatches, then switch back once runners are set. I'll open a tiny PR to tweak the workflow for the onboarding branch.

Ruth: requested Buildkite App install for client-examples and added Zoe to infra-ci team. FYI if your GitHub org uses SSO you may need to reauthorize the Buildkite App after we add you to the team.

Zoe: reauthorized and retried. Buildkite now advances but fails during the image push with: 
```
Error response from daemon: Get https://gcr.io/v2/: denied: Token exchange failed for service account
```

Kobe: that one is IAM-scoped: CI service account needs permission to push to GCR (roles/storage.admin or the narrower set of storage.objects.create + storage.objects.delete + storage.objects.get). Our onboarding pipeline normally skips the push or uses a fake push to a local registry to avoid needing cloud creds.

Zoe: oh neat. I didn't expect cloud creds to be required for the sample. for now i'll skip the push.

ci-bot: Buildkite: pipeline "client-examples/onboard" started on agent group: general; job failed on step: docker-push (401).

Nima: I've pushed the ubuntu-latest tweak and a change that disables the push for branches in the onboarding/* namespace. that should let you validate the tests without credentials.

Zoe: GH Action re-run still complained about secrets missing even after I was added to infra-ci. I checked and repo-level Actions permissions were set to Read-only. changed to Read and write, reran and the job picked up secrets after a maintainer approved the environment. :relieved:

Ruth: quick summary for the docs (adding to docs/onboarding/ci.md): 1) Ensure Buildkite GitHub App installed or use deploy key. 2) New hires should branch in-repo until infra-ci membership propagates. 3) Check Actions -> Environments for required reviewers which block secrets. 4) Runner labels must match self-hosted runners; use ubuntu-latest for onboarding. 5) CI cloud pushes (GCR/GCR) need service account permissions; onboarding pipelines skip pushes by default. 6) If org uses SSO, reauthorize GitHub Apps after team additions.

Zoe: build finally green after skipping the push and workflow tweak! thanks everyone. would love a 15m walkthrough on CI next week to avoid repeating these gotchas.

Kobe: welcome aboard Zoe, adding a quick CI onboarding slot to your calendar. ping @ruth if you want the doc link. :coffee:
